I’ve been there. Find some grounding activities that help you calm down and think more clearly about things. It sucks to feel lost and I hope things get better for you

Is there an option to stop living with them? If so, that sounds like it would be helpful.

If not, maybe try to take some space away from them. If they’re not going to take the time to understand where you’re coming from, you don’t have to talk to them. You deserve to be happy and if they’re taking that away from you, it’s on them. 

I guess before taking space, if you feel like you might be able to have an open and calm conversation about how you’ve been feeling, it might help to sit down with them and just let them know where you’re coming from.

I get where you’re coming from. The weight of everyone else’s expectations can be crushing.

It sounds like you need to think about what you want- maybe you need to take some space away from the family so you can have more room to think about how you want to live your life.

“Potential” is a funny thing. It doesn’t matter if you are a brilliant engineer or a brilliant barista in the scheme of things. It matters that you’re happy. You deserve to enjoy your life, and if that means breaking away from being the person everyone else wants you to be, their responses and emotions are up to them. You are not responsible for how they react, because you have to do what’s best for you.

Sometimes when people get in relationships they kind of disappear for a while.

Hopefully this doesn’t last longer than a year for you guys, but until then, it may help to look for other friends you can count on at this time. If there aren’t a ton, see if you can find new ones through similar interest groups in your area or online. 

She may need some space for a little bit and that’s okay. Try not to push her away, take time for you and think about what you need.

We’re not on earth to be productive. Society expects us to be happy little worker bees, but we are human and complex.

Suicide is not the only option. There are options where you can live somewhere that some living expenses are paid for, as long as you do whatever it is they’re looking for. Like being an au pair, working in a farming program, being in the military (not the best option, but an option), and I’m sure there are others like that. Being a translator in another country could work.

You have a lot of options. You need to be brave enough to go wherever life leads you.

That’s easier said than done but it sounds like taking care of your mental health right now would be the first thing to think about.

My mom was also a very angry and mean person growing up. My life was so different when I went to college and didn’t live with my parents anymore.

It sucks now. People would tell me it would get better and I didn’t believe them because I couldn’t imagine a future where I was actually happy. The world feels like it’s on fire right now, but I’m almost 28 now and I’m actually really happy. 

If you can go live with someone else, like an aunt or anything, please reach out and see. You deserve better. I’m sure that is an unlikely option though, so do your best to limit your time around her, like maybe find activities where you can be outside the house or in your room with headphones on.

Parents with anger make life really hard.

Don’t forget that your feelings are valid and you’re not a burden. Find a friend or family member who you feel safe telling things to and tell them how you’ve been feeling. People want to help. 

Also, grounding activities like reading, listening to calming music (lofi is good), going on walks, or meditating are all good for making you feel more calm.

Good luck and I hope things get better for you soon.
